item.title: Indian refiners' fuel exports to West rise 43% amid Russian crude use
item.description: Refineries in India and two other countries that run on Russian crude shipped 1 billion euros (USD 1.2 billion) of oil products to sanctioning countries in September, up 43 per cent from August, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). Reliance Industries Ltd's Jamnagar refinery in Gujarat supplied six of the seven cargoes unloaded at EU ports that month, despite the bloc's ban on fuel made from Russian crude. The CREA report covers refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei. The EU took 667 million euros' worth of their products, Australia 168 million euros, the US 154 million euros and New Zealand 19 million euros. CREA estimated 295 million euros' worth was refined from Russian crude. Jamnagar also supplied the group's largest US-bound exports, worth 122 million euros, and Russian crude made up 32 per cent of its imports from July to September. item.description: Delhi government has set up Delhi Institute for Transformation and Innovation (DITI) on the lines of NITI Aayog, for policy-making under its goal of "Viksit Dilli by 2047", officials said on Saturday. DITI will function as the Delhi government's premier advisory body for public policy, development strategy and institutional reforms, an official notification said. DITI replaces the Dialogue and Development Commission (DDC) that previously served as the think tank of the city government under AAP rule. item.title: India to keep Russian oil imports near current levels after Trump waiver
item.description: India is expected to keep importing Russian crude at close to current levels after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs mandated by a new law on major buyers of Russian oil, analysts said. Trump issued an executive order late on Friday waiving the "sanctions, restrictions, and duties" under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a day before a 30-day deadline for enforcement expired. He signed the law on September 18. The law authorised tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude and gas, and sanctions on Russia's shadow fleet of tankers. The waiver is not specific to India and could also benefit China. The order lets the administration reconsider it later. India is the largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day this year, ahead of China at 1.2 million, ship tracking data showed. item.title: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
item.description: The Indian economy is expected to grow by 7.1-7.3 per cent in the current fiscal, with a sustained revival in private investment providing an additional source of demand, Deloitte India said on Friday. However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added. Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion. "The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said. Deloitte Economic Outlook

item.title: Current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August: RBI data
item.description: India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data released by the RBI on Thursday. The net deficit in the merchandise trade account declined to USD 26.6 billion in August from USD 27.6 billion in the same month last year. Merchandise exports rose to USD 44.7 billion in August from USD 35.1 billion a year ago, while imports increased to USD 71.3 billion from USD 62.7 billion, the RBI data showed. The surplus in services trade increased to USD 16.5 billion in August from USD 15.6 billion a year ago. Services exports rose to USD 35.5 billion from USD 31.2 billion, while imports increased to USD 18.9 billion from USD 15.6 billion. Net transfers, including remittances, increased to USD 12.8 billion in August from USD 12.2 billion a year ago, while the net deficit in the income account widened to USD 8 billion from USD 6.3 .

item.title: Net direct tax collection grows 13% to ₹13.38 trillion till October 14
item.description: Net direct tax collection rose 13.21 per cent to about Rs 13.38 lakh crore between April 1 and October 14, driven by a healthy pick-up in corporate taxes. Net corporate tax mop-up grew 20.58 per cent to over Rs 5.99 lakh crore, while non-corporate tax (paid by individuals, firms and HUFs) rose 5.83 per cent to about Rs 6.92 lakh crore so far this fiscal year. Collection from securities transaction tax (STT) swelled 52 per cent to Rs 46,840 crore till October 14 of FY27. Refund issuances soared 24.22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.65 lakh crore during the period. On a gross basis, direct tax collection rose 15 per cent to Rs 16.03 lakh crore till October 14. This included corporate tax collection of Rs 7.53 lakh crore and non-corporate tax of Rs 8.03 lakh crore.
